title: Finite infinitesimal neighborhoods detect a smooth connected subgroup normalizer
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and let $G\to S$ be a smooth affine group scheme of finite presentation [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. A group scheme over $S$ is a group object in schemes over $S$ [def-pc-scheme], with multiplication, identity and inverse as in [def-sc-group-scheme], over this base. Let $H\hookrightarrow G$ be a finitely presented closed subgroup [def-weil-closed-immersion], smooth with nonempty geometrically connected fibres [def-weil-connected-scheme]; geometrically connected means connected after extension of the residue field to an algebraic closure. For $K=G,H$, let $I_K$ be the ideal sheaf of its identity section and put $K_n=V(I_K^{n+1})$ for $n\geq1$, the closed subscheme defined by this ideal power. Then $G_n$ and $H_n$ are finite locally free over $S$ [def-pc-finite-locally-free], their coordinate algebras are finite locally free modules (Zariski locally finite free), and their formation commutes with arbitrary base change. Conjugation on $G$ preserves $G_n$, and $H_n\hookrightarrow G_n$ induces a surjection of these coordinate algebras. There is a finite cover of $S$ by affine open subschemes $U_i$ [def-weil-open-immersion] and integers $n_i\geq1$ such that the coordinate algebras $C_i$ of $(G_{n_i})_{U_i}$ and $D_i$ of $(H_{n_i})_{U_i}$ are free of finite constant ranks $M_i$ and $r_i$, respectively, with $1\leq r_i\leq M_i$. For every $U_i$-scheme $W$ and every $g\in G(W)$ one has
$$c_g((H_{n_i})_W)=(H_{n_i})_W\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad c_g(H_W)=H_W.$$
Equalities here are equalities of closed subschemes; $c_g$ denotes conjugation and $K_W=K\times_SW$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. The same equivalence, and the quotient $C_i\twoheadrightarrow D_i$, remain valid after any base change of $U_i$. No self-normalizer hypothesis on $H$ and no connectedness hypothesis on $G$ is imposed.

source.place: Conrad, Reductive group schemes, Proposition 2.1.6 and proof, printed pp.61-63 (finite flat infinitesimal neighborhoods and universal weak schematic density); Theorem 2.3.6 proof, printed p.74, first two paragraphs (stabilization of the finite-jet normalizers). Arbitrary-ring formulation uses the finite-presentation limit reduction stated in both proofs, before finite Zariski trivialization of the jet algebras. Read online; WANTED locally as literature/conrad-reductive-group-schemes.pdf. No Stacks tag states this combined finite-jet normalizer assertion.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-smooth-section-finite-jets] to the identity sections of $G$ and $H$. Both schemes are smooth affine of finite presentation, and the identity gives the required algebra retraction. It follows that all $G_n,H_n$ are finite locally free, and their coordinate quotients commute with arbitrary affine base change. For a general base change these identifications agree on affine overlaps because they preserve the quotient maps, so they glue. By [def-pc-finite-locally-free] the structural maps are finite, flat and locally finitely presented. Apply [lem-pc-finite-flat-pushforward-locally-free] with the rank-one module $\mathcal O_{K_n}$, for $K=G,H$. Its conclusion says precisely that the coordinate algebra of $K_n$ is a finite locally free module on $S$.

source.place: Proposition 2.1.6 proof, pp.62--63; Theorem 2.3.6 proof, p.74, finite locally free coordinate algebras. Module interpretation also follows from Stacks Tag 02KB (morphisms-lemma-finite-flat).

proof.text: Write $G=\operatorname{Spec}B$, $H=\operatorname{Spec}D$ and let $q:B\twoheadrightarrow D$ be the quotient supplied by [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Let $J_G,J_H$ be the augmentation ideals and $Q=\ker q$. Compatibility with identity gives $q(J_G)=J_H$: a lift of any element of $J_H$ already has augmentation zero. Consequently $\mathcal O(H_n)=D/J_H^{n+1}=B/(Q+J_G^{n+1})$ is a quotient of $B/J_G^{n+1}$. More generally $H\cap G_m=H_m$ and $H_n\cap G_m=H_m$ for $n\geq m$, since the sum of the corresponding ideals is $Q+J_G^{m+1}$. These calculations hold after every base change by step 1. For every test scheme $T$ and $g\in G(T)$, $c_g$ fixes the identity section, so its pullback preserves $J_{G_T}$ and each power. Its inverse is $c_{g^{-1}}$, so it preserves $(G_m)_T$ as a closed subscheme. Applying this to the universal element over $G$ proves preservation by the conjugation action itself.

source.place: Theorem 2.3.6 proof, p.74, quotient algebras and conjugation action; elementary augmentation-ideal calculation.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-smooth-connected-subgroup-noetherian-model] choose $A_0\subset A$, $S_0=\operatorname{Spec}A_0$, and compatible models $H_0\hookrightarrow G_0$ for the entire group and subgroup data. In particular $A_0$ and $G_0$ are Noetherian, $G_0$ is smooth affine of finite presentation, and $H_0$ is smooth with nonempty geometrically connected fibers. Perform steps 1--2 over this model. Denote its jets by $G_{0,n},H_{0,n}$. All tests in steps 4--7 will be arbitrary $S_0$-schemes; they are not required to be Noetherian. This universal test statement is what will allow return to $A$ in step 8.

source.place: Proposition 2.1.6 proof, p.62, simultaneous noetherian reduction; Theorem 2.3.6 proof, pp.73--74.

proof.text: For each $n\geq1$, apply [lem-sfb-finite-locally-free-source-factorization-locus] twice with finite locally free source $H_{0,n}$, parameter $P=G_0$, affine finitely presented target $X=G_0$, and finitely presented closed target $Z=H_0$. The two families send $(h,g)$ to $ghg^{-1}$ and $g^{-1}hg$. Obtain closed loci $L_n^+,L_n^-\hookrightarrow G_0$. Write $G_0=\operatorname{Spec}C_0$ and $L_n^\pm=\operatorname{Spec}(C_0/K_n^\pm)$ using [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Set $K_n=K_n^++K_n^-$ and $N_n=\operatorname{Spec}(C_0/K_n)$. On an affine test, factoring through $N_n$ means killing both ideals, hence imposing both containment conditions $c_g((H_{0,n})_T)\subseteq(H_0)_T$ and $c_{g^{-1}}((H_{0,n})_T)\subseteq(H_0)_T$. For general tests the same characterization holds: local quotient factorizations are unique and agree on overlaps, and [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing] glues them. The factorization-locus lemma is valid for arbitrary tests and arbitrary base change, so this construction does not merely characterize geometric points.

source.place: Lemma 2.1.3 and proof, pp.58--59; Proposition 2.1.2 proof, p.60, coefficient-equation loci; Theorem 2.3.6 proof, p.74, closed jet normalizers. Gluing: Stacks Tags 01JA and 04TN.

proof.text: Since $c_g$ preserves $(G_{0,n})_T$, step 2 identifies the two containment conditions in step 4 with $c_g((H_{0,n})_T)\subseteq(H_{0,n})_T$ and its inverse condition. Applying $c_g$ to the inverse condition gives the reverse inclusion, so $N_n(T)$ is exactly the equality stabilizer of $(H_{0,n})_T$. Moreover preservation of $H_{0,n}$ implies preservation of $H_{0,m}=H_{0,n}\cap G_{0,m}$ for $m\leq n$, by step 2. Thus $N_n$ is a closed subfunctor of $N_m$. In particular $K_m\subseteq K_n$: evaluate this functorial containment on the universal point of $\operatorname{Spec}(C_0/K_n)$ to see that its quotient map kills $K_m$. This proves the descending-chain assertion scheme-theoretically, rather than from containment of the jets alone.

source.place: Theorem 2.3.6 proof, p.74, descending intersection; explicit verification using the ambient augmentation filtration.

proof.text: For an arbitrary $T$ and $g$ lying in all $N_n(T)$, form in $(H_0)_T$ the inverse image of $(H_0)_T\hookrightarrow(G_0)_T$ under $c_g|_{(H_0)_T}$. It is a closed subscheme by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change], and contains every $(H_{0,n})_T$, $n\geq1$. It contains the zeroth jet as well, since that factors through the first jet. Apply [lem-sfb-smooth-section-universal-jet-density] to $Y=H_0$ with its identity section: $A_0$ is Noetherian, and $H_0$ is affine smooth of finite presentation with nonempty geometrically connected fibers. The inverse image is the whole of $(H_0)_T$. Thus $c_g((H_0)_T)\subseteq(H_0)_T$. Applying the same argument to $g^{-1}$ gives the reverse inclusion, hence equality. Conversely, if $c_g$ preserves $(H_0)_T$, it preserves all jets by intersecting with $(G_{0,n})_T$. Therefore $\bigcap_{n\geq1}N_n(T)=\{g:c_g((H_0)_T)=(H_0)_T\}$ on every test, including nonreduced and non-Noetherian tests.

source.place: Proposition 2.1.6 proof, pp.62--63, universal weak schematic density; Theorem 2.3.6 proof, p.74. Closed inverse images: Stacks Tag 01QR.

proof.text: By [pqf-lem-affine-open-locnoeth], $C_0$ is Noetherian because $G_0$ is Noetherian and affine. Put $K=\sum_{n\geq1}K_n$. By [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] choose finitely many generators of $K$. Each generator is a finite sum of elements of finitely many $K_n$, and the ideals increase by step 5. Choose $N\geq1$ at least all these indices (take $N=1$ if there are no generators). Then $K=K_N$. For every test $T$, factoring through $\operatorname{Spec}(C_0/K)$ is equivalent to factoring through every $N_n$: on affine opens it means that the ring map kills every $K_n$, and the unique local factorizations glue as in step 4. Since $K=K_N$, step 6 identifies $N_N(T)$ with the normalizer of $(H_0)_T$ on all tests. No inference from stabilization of underlying closed sets is used.

source.place: Theorem 2.3.6 proof, p.74, noetherian stabilization. Stacks Tag 00FM (algebra-section-Noetherian), finite generation of every ideal.

proof.text: Regard any $S$-scheme $W$ as an $S_0$-scheme. The compatible model isomorphisms of step 3 identify $(G_0)_W=G_W$ and $(H_0)_W=H_W$, preserving conjugation. Step 1 identifies $(H_{0,N})_W=(H_N)_W$. Hence step 7 gives $c_g((H_N)_W)=(H_N)_W$ if and only if $c_g(H_W)=H_W$ for every $W$ and $g\in G(W)$. The identical argument applies when $W$ is a scheme over any base change $S'\to S$. Thus the same single integer $N$ detects the normalizer over $S$ and after every base change, without descent of a pre-existing normalizer and without a flatness hypothesis on the base change.

source.place: Theorem 2.3.6 proof, pp.73--74, return from the noetherian model; universal-test interpretation.

proof.text: By step 1 the coordinate modules of $G_N,H_N$ are finite locally free. Simultaneously trivialize them on affine principal opens $U_i=D(f_i)\subseteq S$, with constant finite ranks $M_i,r_i$ on each. One may take finitely many such opens: a principal-open cover means the $f_i$ generate the unit ideal, so an expression $1=\sum_{i\in F}a_if_i$ selects a finite subcover. Discard empty opens; if $S$ is empty take the empty cover. Set $n_i=N$. Step 2 supplies a surjection $C_i\twoheadrightarrow D_i$, so on residue fields its source dimension is at least its target dimension, giving $r_i\leq M_i$. The augmentation $D_i\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal O(U_i)$ shows $r_i\geq1$ on a nonempty open. Step 8 supplies the equivalence for every $U_i$-scheme. After arbitrary base change the chosen bases remain bases, and the map remains surjective: a quotient tensored with an algebra is still the quotient by the extended ideal. Step 1 identifies these quotients with the base-changed jets. This proves every base-change and finite-cover clause of the statement.

source.place: Theorem 2.3.6 proof, p.74, local trivialization of the finite locally free jet algebras; elementary principal-open finite selection and residue-field rank inequalities.

proof_origin.place: Expanded argument for Proposition 2.1.6 and Theorem 2.3.6, pp.61--63 and 73--74, read online; local copy requested in report.md.
